text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000512 bills 99215 far above expectation in every complexity stratum, but the returned charts largely support the billed levels, so documentation and claims data point in different directions.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is consistent with upcoding: the elevated 99215 share appears in every complexity band, including patients with no chronic conditions, so sicker patients alone do not explain it. The documentation points the other way, since the 24 documented 99215 claims show an unsupported rate below the comparison providers, and that is a reasonable sample. The key ambiguity is whether those notes reflect real visits. Several supported 99215s are on low-complexity patients documented at high MDM, for example C0275606 (back pain, no chronic conditions, 50 minutes), C0275317 (obesity only) and C0275529 (type 2 diabetes only). Together with the problem-list flags (e.g., C0275216, C0275317), the repeated-time signal and the few data-reviewed notes with no lab line, this is weak evidence of templated or inflated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first audit the low-complexity 99215 notes clinically to see whether the documented high MDM is credible, and should request the EHR audit trail, which was not received, to check for cloning or after-the-fact edits."}
